sources.note: Lewo Eleng [lwe] appears only in the classification tree (East Lamaholot: Lamatuka, Lewo Eleng; p.166) and comparative lexical tables (data from Fricke 2019, Keraf 1978). Sec. 3.2.1.2 'Schwa' (pp.114-115) gives an areal remark only: 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables.' No Lewo Eleng-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Keraf, Gregorius. 1978. Morfologi Dialek Lamalera (Daftar Kata Dasar, pp.406-447). Doctoral dissertation, Universitas Indonesia, Jakarta. [Lewoeleng 200-item wordlist as digitized in LexiRumah 3, lect lama1277-lewoe]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist only (199 forms). Keraf's orthography uses acute accents for vowel quality (e = schwa vs e-acute = [e], e.g. ile-acute 'mountain' = /ile/, elen = /schwa-l-e~/), plus glottal stop and nasal vowels; no stress marking. The dissertation text itself (print, UI) could not be opened.

sources.citation: Fricke, Hanna L. 2019. Traces of language contact: The Flores-Lembata languages in eastern Indonesia. LOT Dissertation Series 544. Utrecht: LOT (Leiden PhD).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 4.1.5 p.160: 'Until today, Eastern Lamaholot remains largely undescribed. The only materials available on Eastern Lamaholot are two 200 items wordlists collected by Keraf (1978a) of the varieties Lewoeleng and Lamatuka.' Fn.4 p.345-6: her own 2017 Lewoeleng data = a few sentences written down by a speaker, phonemes uncertain. Stress is described only for CL-Central Lembata (sec. 3.2.5 p.49: penultimate, ultimate if penult is schwa) -- a different language (Central Lamaholot, lvu). Nothing on Lewoeleng stress.
